name: Tyler Hoffman
headline: 23, overnight home-care aide, Columbus, Ohio
title: Overnight Shift Request
situation: It's 5:30 a.m. on a Tuesday. Tyler has just finished repositioning Roy and checking his vitals during his overnight shift. Roy is asleep. The phone rings; it's the agency coordinator, saying the daytime aide called in sick and they need Tyler to stay until noon. Tyler has his first phlebotomy class at the vocational center at 8 a.m. The coordinator asks him right now if he can cover. Tyler has only a few seconds to answer.

context.relationship_profiles: Roy is his regular client; Tyler knows his night rhythm and Roy has thanked him for showing up on time, and Tyler avoids prying into his war stories. The agency coordinator has adjusted Tyler's shift schedule twice already to fit his phlebotomy classes, so she is aware of his 8 a.m. commitment. The phlebotomy instructor has a reputation for being strict, and Tyler has not met her yet.
context.tendencies: He dropped the CNA class after three weeks when it felt like school, and he left the computer science program mid-semester after months of mental checkout. He has repeatedly rearranged his overnight shifts with the agency to keep the phlebotomy schedule open. He often makes verbal plans and lets them fade quietly, leaving half-used notebooks with lists he never completes.
context.current_state: Tyler is on hour seven of the overnight shift, physically tired but alert after repositioning Roy. He has been looking forward to the first phlebotomy class all week and left his notebook with the syllabus on the kitchen counter. His parents' coverage of his bills means no financial pressure is pushing him either way this morning.
context.immediate_memories: The agency coordinator's voice on the phone reminds him of the two calls he made to rearrange his shift for the phlebotomy program. The mention of the daytime aide calling in sick brings back the night Jake backed out and Tyler filled in for Roy on a whim.
context.reflective_memories: He remembers dropping the CNA class because the textbook diagrams pulled him back to sleeping through high school biology. He thinks about how Roy still does his daily exercises without anyone watching, and he has noticed he respects that in Roy more than he respects his own follow-through.
